definition: Adding intermediate rewards to guide learning when the true reward is sparse.
details: Adding intermediate rewards to guide learning when the true reward is sparse. Helpful and dangerous in equal measure: badly shaped rewards teach the shaping, not the goal.

explainer.lead: Reward shaping adds intermediate rewards to guide learning when the true reward is sparse. It is helpful and dangerous in equal measure.

tiers.eli5: When the real prize is rare, you hand out small prizes along the way to keep the learner moving in the right direction.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add stepwise rewards to speed up learning in sparse-reward tasks. The pitfall is that badly shaped rewards teach the shaping, not the goal.
tiers.paperLevel: Augmenting the original reward with additional intermediate reward terms to make learning tractable under sparse feedback; effectiveness depends on the added terms not distorting the true objective.

explainer.example: A maze-solving agent gets a small reward for each step toward the exit; if shaped poorly, it may learn to hover near the exit without ever leaving.
